alignments.note: Rule 17 heads the support-verb rendering on the meaning-bearing complement *diligence*. The supplied complementizer introduces the infinitive's own English clause and is its helper, not this verb's (rules 7, 40, 61), as PHP.4.14, TIT.1.16, 2CO.10.7, 2CO.11.5 and EPH.4.17 place it; rule 74's closing aside rests on JHN.5.39 alone, which is itself medium and concedes the infinitive.
Intensifying kai; the ASV writes no word for it (rule 65).
One Greek adverb rendered by a phrase; 'time' glosses the temporal element of hekastote, so rule 66 heads there, though 'every' remains defensible.

The infinitive is rendered as a finite clause and the supplied complementizer is its helper, discontinuously under rule 15 across the adverbial phrase and the expressed accusative subject, which aligns separately (rules 7, 40). Rule 17 heads on the lexical *able* rather than the modal or copula. As at 2PE.1.19, where the participle likewise carries its own *that*.
The first-person possessive adjective carries 'my', so the article realizes nothing (rules 54, 20).
Infinitival 'to' is the verb's own helper, no conjunction governing the clause (rules 7, 40).
Article governing mnemen across the interposed genitive (rule 57); the ASV supplies no determiner, so it realizes nothing (rule 23).
Rule 17 heads the substantival demonstrative on 'these', the supplied 'things' completing it.
The ASV spells both elements of the light-verb pair out, so it splits under rule 2; 'to' is the noun's case helper.
